reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: The trial measured CD8+ T cell responses by ELISPOT as the primary endpoint, which directly assesses whether the peptide vaccines engaged their intended targets (tumor antigens). The primary endpoint was not met, suggesting limited target engagement. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: While CD4+CD25+FoxP3+ regulatory T cells were monitored and gene expression profiles analyzed, no specific biomarker changes confirming downstream immune activation were reported. The lack of robust CD8+ T cell responses suggests the immune costimulation pathway was not effectively modulated. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Both arms failed on PFS (130 days vaccine alone vs 64 days vaccine+IL-12), with the IL-12 combination actually performing worse. OS also failed in the vaccine+IL-12 arm (199 days). No clinical benefit was observed. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses were reported, so differential responses cannot be assessed. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial was terminated early due to lack of clinical efficacy and drug supply issues. The small sample size (N=10) suggests the study was underpowered. Additionally, there was a Grade 5 death in the IL-12 arm, indicating safety concerns.
